rationale: The records exist for every referral, the question is a comparison of settings patients already chose, and no new data can be collected, so a retrospective comparison of programme records fits. It must apply one attendance-equivalent completion definition (claim c2), keep non-starters in both denominators, and adjust for distance (claim c3) and other referral factors, because the published choice-based difference (claim c1) was distorted by exactly these problems.
alternatives: Randomise new referrals between settings (refused: the board wants an answer by April 2027 and patients value choice)
Crude completion by programme (refused: confounded and inconsistently defined)
whyNotMoreComplex: A target trial emulation with time-varying exposure is unnecessary because the exposure is fixed at choice; one adjusted model and a sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding answer the board's question.

decision.statement: Compare completion between remote and centre-based rehabilitation for all 1,146 referrals from 2023 to 2025 from programme records, applying one attendance-equivalent completion definition to both programmes, adjusting for the factors recorded at referral and reporting results by sex, age, deprivation and distance.
decision.question: Is completion of remote rehabilitation different from centre-based rehabilitation in this programme, and for whom?

criteria.text: A difference in completion between settings is plausible in a choice-based service and large enough to matter to the board.
A single definition applied to both programmes and distance adjustment are needed for a fair comparison.
The records cannot identify which patients were offered both programmes.

gates.requirement: Information governance approval to access the programme records
gates.evidence: Approval IG-CR-2026-19 dated 2026-08-27, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Research ethics decision on secondary use without consent
gates.evidence: Waiver of consent REB-2026-331 dated 2026-09-15, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Report crude completion by programme without adjustment
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records; both gates rest on the investigator's approvals.

summary: Retrospective comparison recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and both gates are met.
